title: Shared ULA beam codebook with sector phase Views
hypothesis: A shared 8-beam ULA codebook plus one sector phase-ramp address preserves simulated sector throughput at lower serialized state than independent sector codebooks; a native sector-indexed steering-code control tests whether this is Mirror-specific.
scope: Synthetic clustered narrowband ULA channels; not a public measured channel dataset, 3GPP conformance model, or network field trial.

system.channel: one LOS path plus three random clustered paths, sector-centered azimuths

storage.authority: actual torch.save decoded inference state, including codebook, sector addresses, metadata and router

compute: Report complex MAC proxy for beam scoring and phase operations. This is simulation only; no radio energy/latency claim.
success_gate: Mirror retains >=95% of independent-codebook mean spectral efficiency in every fresh world and uses <=50% of its serialized beam-state bytes; native sector-address control must be separately evaluated.
failure_gate: Any fresh world misses quality/storage gate or Mirror aliases the native sector steering-code control.
boundaries: No realistic pilot/coherence feedback overhead modeled beyond beam-index bits.
No measured spectral efficiency, RF energy, switching latency, or field generalization.
